title: Farmers department store staff strike over pay in New Zealand
seoTitle: Auckland Farmers staff strike over pay

tea.why: Workers are striking due to a 2.5% pay offer that they state is below inflation, alongside concerns regarding performance-based pay systems.
tea.want: The union is demanding fair wages and improved working conditions to address the cost-of-living crisis.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Over 1,300 staff participated in a two-hour walkout across multiple cities, including Auckland, Hamilton, and Christchurch.

summary: On November 26, 2026, more than 1,300 employees of the Farmers Trading Company held a two-hour strike across several New Zealand cities, including Auckland, Hamilton, Tauranga, Wellington, Christchurch, and Dunedin. Organised by the Workers First Union, the action was timed for the day before Black Friday and dubbed 'Black Thursday'. Workers are protesting against a 2.5% pay increase offer, which they describe as a real-term pay cut amid a cost-of-living crisis. The union also criticised the company's performance-based pay system. According to the Workers First regional organising director, Kristin Miller, five months of collective bargaining have failed to meet staff demands for fair wages. No official response from the Farmers Trading Company or the James Pascoe Group was reported in the provided sources.
demands: Removal of the performance-based pay system
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: More than 1300 Farmers Trading Company staff

updates.text: Over 1,300 staff walked off the job for two hours in multiple cities to protest pay offers and performance-based pay systems.
